ai.definition: DeepSeek AI is an advanced form of artificial intelligence infrastructure that utilizes deep learning techniques to analyze large and complex datasets with high speed and precision.
ai.howItWorks: DeepSeek AI employs neural networks, particularly deep neural networks (DNNs), to process and interpret vast amounts of data. These networks are designed to mimic the structure and function of the human brain, allowing for hierarchical feature extraction and pattern recognition from raw input data.
ai.problemSolved: The technology addresses the challenge of extracting meaningful insights from large, complex datasets that traditional computing methods struggle with due to their volume, velocity, or variety (3Vs).
ai.manufacturing: Manufacturing DeepSeek AI involves developing and training neural networks on high-performance hardware such as GPUs and TPUs. The process includes data preprocessing, model architecture design, training, validation, and deployment.
ai.buildProcess: The build process for DeepSeek AI begins with collecting and preparing large datasets relevant to the application domain (e.g., medical records in healthcare). These datasets are then fed into a neural network that is iteratively trained using algorithms like backpropagation. Once the model reaches satisfactory performance, it undergoes validation on unseen data before deployment.
ai.costDrivers: Key cost drivers include the expense of high-performance computing resources for training and inference, the quality and quantity of labeled datasets required for effective training, and ongoing maintenance costs for software updates and hardware upgrades.
ai.lifecycleOutlook: The outlook suggests continued growth as more industries recognize the value in leveraging AI for data analysis. However, challenges such as regulatory compliance and ethical considerations may slow adoption in certain sectors.
ai.regulation: Regulations vary by industry and region but generally focus on ensuring data privacy, transparency of algorithms, and accountability in decision-making processes involving AI systems.
ai.risks: Risks include potential bias in training datasets leading to unfair or discriminatory outcomes, cybersecurity threats to sensitive data, and the need for ongoing model updates as new data becomes available.
ai.profitability: Profitability is high due to the demand for advanced analytics solutions but can be impacted by factors such as competition from other AI providers and the cost of maintaining cutting-edge infrastructure.
ai.futureDevelopment: Future development may involve advancements in explainable AI, integration with edge computing for real-time decision-making, and the use of quantum computing to further enhance processing capabilities.

glossary.def: A class of artificial neural networks that can learn complex patterns in data through multiple layers of processing.
Computational resources designed to perform intensive computing tasks, often used for training and inference of AI models.

subsystems.name: Tokenizer and embeddings
subsystems.role: turns raw text into the integer tokens the network actually processes.

subsystems.name: Attention layers
subsystems.role: let every token weigh every other token in the context.
parts: multi-head latent attention with a compressed key-value cache

subsystems.name: Mixture-of-experts feedforward layers
subsystems.role: provide most of the model's stored knowledge while only activating a slice per token.
parts: router that picks a few experts per token

subsystems.name: Training stack
subsystems.role: runs the pretraining job across thousands of accelerators.

subsystems.name: Post-training and reasoning
subsystems.role: turns a text predictor into something that reasons and follows instructions.

subsystems.name: Inference and serving
subsystems.role: delivers the model cheaply enough to be used at scale.

buildSteps.title: Assemble the training corpus
buildSteps.detail: Crawl and licence text and code, then filter, deduplicate and quality-score it — the published pretraining run consumed on the order of 15 trillion tokens.

buildSteps.title: Train the tokenizer
buildSteps.detail: Fit a byte-level vocabulary of roughly 128,000 tokens so common words and code fragments become single units.

buildSteps.title: Pretrain the base model
buildSteps.detail: Predict the next token over the corpus on a large cluster of accelerators, training in 8-bit floating point and routing each token to a few experts out of many, in a model with about 671 billion parameters of which roughly 37 billion are active per token.

buildSteps.title: Supervised fine-tuning
buildSteps.detail: Train on curated instruction-and-answer pairs so the model responds usefully rather than just continuing text.

buildSteps.title: Reinforcement learning for reasoning
buildSteps.detail: Generate many candidate solutions to maths, code and logic problems, automatically check which answers are correct, and reinforce the paths that got there — letting a reasoning mode emerge without human-written chain-of-thought examples.

buildSteps.title: Distil smaller models
buildSteps.detail: Use the large model's outputs to train compact dense models that run on modest hardware.

buildSteps.title: Evaluate and red-team
buildSteps.detail: Benchmark reasoning, coding and multilingual ability, and probe for harmful or unsafe outputs.

buildSteps.title: Serve and iterate
buildSteps.detail: Quantise the weights, run them behind an API or release them openly, and collect feedback for the next training round.

prerequisites.tech: High-performance GPU accelerators and fast interconnect
prerequisites.why: pretraining is limited by how many chips can be kept busy at once; export controls have shaped which chips are available.
a single model cannot fit on one device, so parallelism and fault recovery are essential.

prerequisites.tech: Web-scale, well-filtered text and code corpora
prerequisites.why: capability scales with the quality and diversity of the pretraining data.
halves memory and speeds up arithmetic relative to 16-bit training.
reinforcement learning works well where answers can be checked by a program or formula, and poorly where quality is subjective.

pathway.milestone: open-weight mixture-of-experts chat and reasoning models released under permissive licences
pathway.unlocks: strong reasoning available to any organisation that can host or call the model.

pathway.milestone: longer context, cheaper inference and more reliable tool use
pathway.unlocks: agents that work through multi-step tasks rather than answering single questions.

pathway.milestone: small distilled models running on phones and laptops
pathway.unlocks: private, low-latency assistants that need no data centre.

pathway.milestone: domain adapters for finance, healthcare and logistics with audit and verification built in
pathway.unlocks: use in regulated work — only where accuracy, provenance and accountability can be demonstrated.
